svg.title: How spans.py lays out masked spans for L = 62 residues and a budget of B = 20
svg.desc: sample_edit_spans_for_budget receives a seed of L = 62 residues and an edit budget of B = 20, which fixes two pools, 20 masked blocks and L - B = 42 kept blocks. Step 1, _sample_truncated_geometric with p = 0.5 draws the span count K once, from 1 to B, where K = 1 has probability 50%, K = 2 25%, K = 3 12.5% and K of 4 or more 12.5%; here K = 2. K feeds two Dirichlet-multinomial draws. Step 2 splits the 20 masked blocks into K = 2 spans, each with at least 1 block, span_0 = 13 and span_1 = 7. Step 3 splits the 42 kept blocks into K + 1 = 3 gaps, gap_0 = 11, gap_1 = 19 and gap_2 = 12, and a gap may be 0. Interleaving [gap_0, span_0, gap_1, span_1, gap_2] gives one 62-residue bar with the half-open spans [(11, 24), (43, 50)]. If an inner gap draws 0, the two spans touch and merge into one, for example (11, 31). sample_edit_masks_for_budgets draws the same layout for a whole batch and returns a boolean mask.
svg.text: Only the two counts are fixed here.
Where the masked residues go comes next.
